Four open PRs do touch the generated `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` — #17914, #17835, #17638 and #17635 — but that file is **deliberately not** a `SINGLE_CLAIM_PATHS` entry: `scripts/check-single-claim-paths.mjs` declares only `.objectui-sha`, and its header states that *"anything that is merely hot (a lock file, a root manifest, **a shared registry**) does NOT belong here … those are ordinary concurrent work"*. ⇒ parallel authoring is legitimate; the **landing** is what serialises, via `bash scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`. No sibling in this epic is dispatched except #17786, whose face is disjoint (it has no rename and does not touch the registry). Lock read `state: lock is free`, `queue: empty` ⇒ arrival depth 1.

### Premise re-measured on `origin/main` @ `84e6b05` (2026-09-13T07:34Z), ⛔ not carried from the card

```
packages/spec/src/system/tenant.zod.ts:446
  schemaCacheTTL: z.number().int().positive().default(3600).describe('Schema cache TTL'),
```

The card's line number (`:446`) **still holds** — no rot. `default(3600)` independently corroborates the JSDoc's "seconds" (3600 s = 1 h; as milliseconds it would be 3.6 s, which is not a schema-cache TTL). The `.describe('Schema cache TTL')` carries no unit, so the row is real.

Unit-suffix convention on `origin/main`, counted here rather than recalled: `…Ms` 109 · `…Seconds` 45 · `…Days` 24 · `…Hours` 4 = **182** keys. This rename joins the `…Seconds` family.

### ⚠️ This card is the epic's pathfinder, and it carries one open measurement

It is the **first of six renames**. Whether a rename is a clause-② widening is, in this repo, a **measurable** question rather than a doctrinal one, and this round is what measures it:

`scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs` declares **T1 — "a new key on a Zod object schema on the contract source surface"**, scoped to `packages/spec/src/**`, whose sentence is *"the accept set gains a spelling an author may now write"*. A rename adds such a spelling. But the same file declares a **REPLACEMENT budget** (from #16943): *"one per change block, per tell kind … buys ONE added line of kind K the right not to be reported"*, and a rename is a deleted `schemaCacheTTL:` line and an added `schemaCacheTtlSeconds:` line in one change block.

⇒ Ruling A's `Clause-②: no` is **plausibly mechanically correct** for a rename, and this claim declares `no` in line with it — but as a declaration to be **tested**, not assumed. The round must report the actual `check-widening-tells` and `check-clause2-carriers --pair` readings for its own diff. If T1 fires and `--pair` returns 4, the `no` is wrong, **this PM flips the declaration for all six rename cards and says so publicly** — ⛔ the dev does not edit this line, and ⛔ the round does not reshape its diff to make a tell go quiet.

⚠️ Regardless of the declaration, the clause-② **path leg** fires on `packages/spec/src/**`, so an in-seat clause-② review record is owed on the PR before it may turn ready or enqueue. Not waived; scheduled.

PM decision, epic PM for the #15939 subtree, `session_015c5G6TmpMKgnusmTpD7Ntt`, 2026-09-13T08:03Z. This supersedes the `Clause-②: no` line in my claim `5651959304`. The dev correctly declined to touch that line and handed the call back — this is that call.

### What the round measured

The pathfinder separated the two halves of a rename on the instrument itself:

| probe | `check-widening-tells` exit | tell |
|:--|--:|:--|
| the rename alone — one key line removed, one added, one change block | **0** | none; the net-delta budget from PR #17216 absorbs it |
| an added `retiredKey(` key line with no paired removal | **4** | T1 on the tombstone |

And on the real pair, read by me rather than reported: `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 17954` ⇒ **exit 4**, C5, one tell, `packages/spec/src/system/tenant.zod.ts:454` `+ schemaCacheTTL: retiredKey(`.

### Why the declaration is `yes` — on the rule, ⛔ not on the checker

The tool's verdict is **not** my reason, and this is the part worth being precise about.

`references/contract-review.md` states a mechanical floor that admits no balancing: *「机械地板 claim 时可查树:新导出符号或**已发布载荷上的新键恒 `yes`**」*. A rename puts `schemaCacheTtlSeconds` — a spelling no author could write before — onto a published payload. That is a new key on a published payload, so the floor reads `yes`.

The same file's conformance clause reaches it a second way: *「conformance 类 ⛔ 不机械化 … 在两个已发布码之间重选输入类都需判断」*, and this lane's own precedent on #16126 records the resolution verbatim — **「重定输入类无论方向都是 `yes`」**. A tenant config carrying `schemaCacheTTL` parses today and is refused after this lands. That is the input class being re-chosen between two published judgments.

⇒ Two independent readings of the governing text give `yes`. The checker's C5 row happens to agree, which is a coincidence of correctness, not the reason.

### ⚠️ This is explicitly NOT the #16943 failure mode, and must not be cited as that precedent

#16943 (now closed, fixed by PR #17216) warned that *「一个 gate whose green is reachable only by lying is worse than one that is merely wrong」* — its case was a **replaced prose string** that widened nothing, where `yes` would have been a false declaration made to satisfy a checker.

This case is the opposite shape: the change **genuinely does** add an authorable spelling to a published payload. Declaring `yes` here is the honest reading of the rule, and it would remain the honest reading if `--pair` returned 0. ⛔ Nobody should read this correction as precedent for re-declaring under checker pressure.

### Relation to Ruling A

Ruling A (batch #115, maintainer 「同意」) prescribes *「each as its own `Clause-②: no` / `patch` round」*. I am changing **only** that classification field, and `references/contract-review.md` is explicit that it is provisional: *「`Clause-②: yes | no` 按设计临时:只定是否必过席内契约复核的保守方向,⛔ 非终审」*.

⛔ Nothing else in Ruling A moves: still **per file**, still **`patch`**, still the #15678/#15679 shape, still PR #17635 **last**. The ruling's `no` was written before the 0→21 measurement existed and before any rename diff had been read on an instrument.

⇒ The practical effect is **more** review, not less, and no rework: clause-② cards are **built at the default tier** (already done — opus) and **reviewed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`**, which the path leg already obliged on every card in this epic.

### Scope of this correction

Applies to all **six rename cards** — #17780, #17781, #17782, #17783, **#17784**, #17785 — because every one carries a `retiredKey()` tombstone and a new suffixed spelling. ⛔ It does **not** apply to #17786 / PR #17953, which adds no key: measured `--pair 17953` ⇒ **exit 0**, and it stays `Clause-②: no`.

`needs:contract-review` is being hung on this card and on PR #17954 as the double carrier, in the same pass.

### On #17955

The round's finding — T1 firing on a `retiredKey()` tombstone, the line that makes the accept set strictly **narrower** — is real, correctly deduped against the closed #17300 and #17618, and ⛔ is **not** what drove this correction. Its sharp edge is a **pure** retirement (a key deleted and tombstoned with no replacement spelling), which widens nothing and would therefore have no honest route to `--pair` 0. This epic never hits that shape; a future retirement card will.
